content.text:
**Verdict: request changes.** I reproduced one regression against main: under `commit.cleanup=scissors` (also `whitespace` or `verbatim`), an editor commit gets a trailer, but post-commit never writes its checkpoint. I haven't applied the /simplify cleanups yet; your working agreement says to wait for approval before editing.

## Brief

**What it does.** Only a commit's last trailer block, read the way git reads it, now decides which checkpoint the commit writes to. That covers prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, amend, attach and `explain --generate`. Read-only lookups still scan the whole message, because squash commits carry their trailers in the body.

The PR also:
- reads git's comment prefix (`core.commentChar`, `core.commentString`, `auto`);
- cuts the message only at the exact scissors line;
- accepts `Key:value` and tab-separated trailers;
- changes how commit-msg decides a message is empty;
- includes #2259's writer fix.

**Why.** An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line pasted, quoted or indented in the body could send a write into an unrelated checkpoint, or into one this clone hasn't fetched.

**Cost and risk.**
- Editor commits, amends and commit-msg each spawn one `git config` (about 3 ms). `-m` commits spawn none.
- The new reader is stricter than git in some message shapes. The PR calls that the safe direction, but for post-commit it isn't (finding 1).

**State.** Head is 4cfd66130 and CI is green. It merges cleanly with upstream/main f36367e6f, whose 3 newer commits don't touch these files. Both Copilot threads are resolved. No Trail exists for this branch, so there were no trail findings to check.

## Findings

### Act on

**1. High, regression: with `commit.cleanup=scissors`/`whitespace`/`verbatim`, the commit gets a trailer but no checkpoint.**
- In these modes git keeps `#` lines, so the commit records Entire's explanation lines inside the trailer paragraph:
  ```
  typed subject

  Entire-Checkpoint: 1e0ed969a3b4
  # Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link ...
  # Last Prompt: change mine.txt
  # The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.
  ```
- `git interpret-trailers --parse` still returns the trailer, because git skips comment lines inside a trailer block.
- [isTrailerBlock](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:440) rejects the whole paragraph, so [stampedTrailersOf](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_provenance.go:221) finds nothing and post-commit writes nothing. The same commit also breaks attach joining and `explain --generate`.
- Evidence: I ran a throwaway integration test through the real hooks (overlay only, nothing written to the repo). It fails on this branch and passes on upstream/main.
- Recommended fix: make the reader skip comment-prefixed lines inside and after the block, as git does. It needs the prefix at read time, and a spawn can be avoided when the message has no `Entire-Checkpoint` key. This covers all three modes and commits already recorded this way.
- Cheaper but partial alternative: write Entire's explanation in its own paragraph above the trailer. It misses `verbatim` when git's comment block is left in, and it misses existing commits.
- Add a scissors row to `TestTrailerAuthority_EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`.

**2. Low-medium: every amend now spawns `git config` before any trailer or session check.** This is at [manual_commit_hooks.go:827](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:827); main spawned nothing there. Skip the spawn when `ParseAllCheckpoints(message)` is empty: every ID the last-block reader accepts also matches that regex. The agent fast path at `:2762` has the same pattern.

### Consider

**3. Low: CRLF scissors lines.** [isScissorsLine](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:180) accepts a CRLF scissors line, but git 2.50 doesn't cut there; I checked, and a CRLF-saved `commit -v` commit records the diff. So the comment "Git cuts only at that exact line" overstates parity. Either drop the `\r` tolerance and its test, or reword the comment.

**4. Follow-up: redo and squash inheritance still scan the whole message.** At [manual_commit_redo.go:69](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_redo.go:69) and [manual_commit_hooks.go:684](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:684), every ID found anywhere in a replaced or squashed commit's message is written into the new commit's last trailer block, which attach and `explain --generate` now trust. A body mention therefore becomes an authoritative trailer one hop later. The PR leaves this alone on purpose, so it's worth a line under "Known gap".

### /simplify: proposed, not applied

These keep behavior the same.
- **S1:** the spawn guard from finding 2.
- **S2:** [checkpointFromTrailerLine](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:155) is a second definition of "checkpoint trailer line" next to `checkpointTrailerLineRegex`. Use the regex so the remover and the readers can't drift apart.
- **S3:** [hasUserContent](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:313) repeats `StripEditorComments`'s comment-dropping loop. Call it when the message ends with git's comment block.
- **S4:** the "writer and readers share one grammar" note appears on both `appendTrailerLine` and `isTrailerBlock`. Keep it on `isTrailerBlock` only.
- **Tests:**
  - Use the existing `keepAll` instead of the new `keepAllTrailers`.
  - In `attach_test.go`, use the existing `readSummary` and `headCommitOf` helpers.
  - Pull the five copies of the prepare-hook run into one `runPrepareCommitMsg` helper.
  - Drop the "passes before and after" note from the `// GUARD:` comment at [checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:240](cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:240); it describes test history, which your comment rule excludes.

Skipped:
- removing `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock`: it mirrors the existing `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints` pair, and removing it churns the tests;
- moving the prefix rules into one `trailers` function: depends on how finding 1 gets fixed;
- reading the config through go-git: it ignores includes and `git -c` overrides;
- bigger redesigns: a cleanup-mode type or a new mention API;
- the double deleted-list read in amend: under 0.1 ms.

## Verification
- **Regression test:** fails on the branch, passes on upstream/main.
- **Real git 2.50 checks:**
  - the scissors-mode commit's trailer is read by `interpret-trailers`;
  - a CRLF scissors line is not cut.
- **Focused tests, all passing:** the `trailers` and `strategy` packages, attach and explain tests in `cli`, and the trailer-authority, adversarial and checkpoint-delete integration tests.
- **Not rerun:** the full `mise run check` (CI is green on this head).

**Review lessons.** I checked the diff against `General.md` and `cli.md`; finding 3 also breaks your Agent Memory rule to state only verified behavior in comments. Proposed new lesson for `General.md`, not added: "When making a parser stricter for safety, check which way is safe for each caller. Rejecting input blocks a write you want to prevent, but it also silently drops a write you need, such as a checkpoint that a trailer git accepts points to."

I put a short version of these findings in the shared notes file `pr-2253-review.md`. The repository is unchanged.

I need to thread ctx through planAttachLink and resolveCheckpointID so they call strategy.FinalCheckpointTrailers with context, and similarly update checkpointForCommit in explain.go to pass ctx and take the first ID returned. For explain, since it resolves commits in the current repo rather than an arbitrary one, there's no `--repo` flag concern, and git invocation already uses exec.CommandContext consistently everywhere, so no changes needed there.

I'm thinking through the efficiency optimization for handleAmendCommitMsg: only compute the stripped-final-trailer prefix when the commit message actually mentions a checkpoint key, then compare live checkpoints after removing deleted ones, falling back to marking strippedDeleted true if nothing remains live. I'm verifying the whole-message regex pattern for checkpoint trailers tolerates trailing carriage returns and correctly matches end-of-string, confirming the fast path is a valid subset of the original matching logic. Verbatim mode would behave like whitespace but skip blank-line collapsing. I'm deciding to add three test rows total: scissors with "#", whitespace with "#", and scissors with ";" as the comment char to exercise prefix plumbing through gitCommentPrefix in post-commit — each is a quick ~1s integration test, which seems reasonable. I'm also recalling the exact wording of git's prepare-commit-msg template text to get the test fixtures right.

I realize the existing assertion (checking that "Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above" is absent) won't work for scissors/whitespace rows, since git's own stripping leaves that explanatory line intact — a separate pre-existing leak I'm not trying to fix here. So these new rows need different assertions, focused only on verifying that post-commit condenses things into the stamped checkpoint and that git's own grammar correctly names the final trailer block; I'm thinking this warrants splitting into its own test function, something like TestTrailerAuth...

I need to enumerate the failure modes before writing any code: trailing comment lines within a paragraph, a trailing comment-only paragraph, comments interspersed between trailers, a comment line followed by indentation that breaks continuation, strict rejection under empty prefix, non-trailing comment paragraphs, and the subject-paragraph exclusion rule. My plan: first empirically verify git's trailer-parsing behavior around comment lines, then write failing unit and integration tests for the grammar and cleanup cases, implement the reader changes to skip comment lines, apply any simplification cleanups, update the docs, run formatting/lint/tests, and finally propose the commit and PR text for approval. This creates a known edge case: if auto-mode wrote a trailer followed by scissors content using ";" comments, a post-commit read with "#" would reject the trailer and leave it uncondensed — but that matches git's own interpret-trailers behavior, so it's acceptable rather than something to special-case. I'm also confirming the no-blank-line and blank-line-before-comment edge cases behave correctly, then moving to check how widely the current API is used before deciding how big this change needs to be.

content.content:
8:## Problem
19:## Cause
23:## Fix
32:Prepare reads the message as git will record it (`trailers.StripEditorComments`): an editor message loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.
38:## Why nothing caught it
42:## Tests, verified RED before the fix
51:- `TestTrailerAuthority_UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` (`;` and `commit -v`) failed with `commit-msg must remove the trailer so git aborts the empty commit`, and `TestTrailerAuthority_MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer` with `commit-msg must keep the trailer of a message with content`. Its default-prefix case is a guard.
53:I also ran a throwaway property check over random messages built from a fixed set of lines (plain, indented, continuation, `#`, CRLF, trailer-shaped subjects). In 20,000 messages the writer's output was always read back by the final-block reader, all 500 sampled outputs parsed in `git interpret-trailers --parse`, and in 1,500 messages the reader never accepted a checkpoint that git rejects. It was stricter than git in 36, which is the safe direction.

fix(trailers): skip comment lines in the final block as git does

With commit.cleanup=scissors or whitespace, git keeps comment lines, so
an editor commit records Entire's explanation inside its trailer
paragraph. git's trailer parser skips those lines, but the final-block
reader rejected the paragraph, so post-commit never wrote the checkpoint
the trailer names.

The reader now skips lines starting with git's comment prefix and
ignores trailing comment lines. Post-commit, attach and explain
--generate read recorded commits through FinalCheckpointTrailers, which
looks the prefix up in git config only when a read without it misses a
checkpoint the message names. The writer still joins only a block
without comment lines.

Amends and editor fast-path commits that name no checkpoint now skip the
git config read. hasUserContent reuses StripEditorComments, the reader
reuses the checkpoint trailer-line regex, and the trailer-authority tests
share one prepare-commit-msg helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

import sys

s = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read()
def rep(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:60]
    s = s.replace(old, new)
rep("The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.",
    "The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.")
rep("Its default-prefix case is a guard.\n",
    "Its default-prefix case is a guard.\n- `TestTrailerAuthority_CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` (`commit.cleanup=scissors` with `#` and `;`, and `whitespace`) failed with `post-commit must condense into the checkpoint the commit's trailer names`, while `git interpret-trailers --parse` read the trailer in each case. `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint` failed with `attach wrote the session into <new id>, want the trailer's checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6`, and the comment-line cases in `trailers_test.go` failed before the reader skipped comment lines.\n")
rep("It was stricter than git in 36, which is the safe direction.",
    "It was stricter than git in 36. Stricter is not always safe, though: with `commit.cleanup=scissors` the reader rejected a trailer git accepts, so post-commit never wrote the checkpoint the trailer names. That case is now covered above.")
rep("and `-m \"#42 fix login\"` keeps its trailer\n",
    "and `-m \"#42 fix login\"` keeps its trailer\n- [x] `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` editor commits link and condense (`TestTrailerAuthority_CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`)\n")
open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
EOF

< Prepare reads the message as git will record it (`trailers.StripEditorComments`): an editor message loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.
---
> Prepare reads the message as git will record it (`trailers.StripEditorComments`): an editor message loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

< I also ran a throwaway property check over random messages built from a fixed set of lines (plain, indented, continuation, `#`, CRLF, trailer-shaped subjects). In 20,000 messages the writer's output was always read back by the final-block reader, all 500 sampled outputs parsed in `git interpret-trailers --parse`, and in 1,500 messages the reader never accepted a checkpoint that git rejects. It was stricter than git in 36, which is the safe direction.

**What changed** (11 files, +350/−248):

  - Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` now read recorded commits through one function, `strategy.FinalCheckpointTrailers`. It only reads `git config` when the message names a checkpoint that a plain read misses, so ordinary post-commits still spawn nothing.
  - The writer still joins only a trailer block with no comment lines.
- **/simplify:**
  - amends and editor fast-path commits that name no checkpoint skip the `git config` read;
  - the reader reuses the existing trailer-line regex;
  - `hasUserContent` reuses `StripEditorComments`;
  - one duplicated doc comment is gone.

**Verification:**
- **Fail before the fix:** the new `TestTrailerAuthority_CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` (scissors with `#` and `;`, and whitespace), `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint`, and 4 new grammar cases all failed. All pass after it.

Two tests failed on timeouts: `TestDiscoverAndRegister_ContinuesAfterRegistrationError` and `TestInstallHooks_ReclaimedChainRunsEachHookOnce`. Both pass when run alone, and the PR doesn't touch either area.

**Proposed commit message:**
```
fix(trailers): skip comment lines in the final block as git does

With commit.cleanup=scissors or whitespace, git keeps comment lines, so
an editor commit records Entire's explanation inside its trailer
paragraph. git's trailer parser skips those lines, but the final-block
reader rejected the paragraph, so post-commit never wrote the checkpoint
the trailer names.

The reader now skips lines starting with git's comment prefix and
ignores trailing comment lines. Post-commit, attach and explain
--generate read recorded commits through FinalCheckpointTrailers, which
looks the prefix up in git config only when a read without it misses a
checkpoint the message names. The writer still joins only a block
without comment lines.

Amends and editor fast-path commits that name no checkpoint now skip the
git config read. hasUserContent reuses StripEditorComments, the reader
reuses the checkpoint trailer-line regex, and the trailer-authority tests
share one prepare-commit-msg helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

content.text:
The new tests failed before the fix because, in commit.cleanup modes other than the default, git keeps Entire's own `#` comment lines inside the commit, and the old reader rejected any trailer paragraph that contained them. Here's the walkthrough with the actual messages from the failing run.

**1. What git hands prepare-commit-msg with `commit.cleanup=scissors`.** In this mode git puts its whole comment block below a scissors line:
```

# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
# Do not modify or remove the line above.
# Everything below it will be ignored.
```

**2. What Entire's prepare-commit-msg writes.** It inserts the trailer plus its explanation above the first `#` line:
```
Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96
# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link ...
# Last Prompt: change mine.txt
# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.

# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
...
```

**3. What git records.** Scissors mode cuts at the scissors line but keeps the `#` lines above it. The default `strip` mode would delete them, which is why this never showed up before:
```
typed in editor

Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96
# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above ...
# Last Prompt: change mine.txt
# The trailer will be added ...
```

**4. Why post-commit wrote nothing.**
- Post-commit asks "which checkpoint did this commit stamp?" and the old reader looked only at the last paragraph: those four lines.
- `isTrailerBlock` required every line to be a trailer or an indented continuation. `# Remove ...` is neither, so it rejected the whole paragraph and returned no trailer.
- With no stamped trailer, post-commit condensed nothing. Checkpoint `cf9aca16fd96` was never written, so `advCheckpointStored` was false: "post-commit must condense into the checkpoint the commit's trailer names."

**5. Why git still sees the trailer.** Git's trailer parser skips comment lines, so `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns `Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96`. The test checks that first, to prove the commit really is linked by git's rules and the failure is in Entire's reader.

**The other rows:**
- **`whitespace`:** git also keeps its own `# Please enter the commit message…` block, so the last paragraph was pure comments and the old reader found no trailer.
- **`;` prefix:** same as the scissors row, with `;` lines.

**The other new tests:**
- **Attach test:** same cause. Attach read the last block, rejected it, and minted a new ID instead of joining: "attach wrote the session into 78219153be59, want the trailer's checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6".
- **Grammar unit cases:** with the prefix ignored, the 4 comment-line cases failed for the same reason.

**Why main passed:** main's post-commit scanned the whole message with a regex, so it found the trailer line no matter what followed it. This PR's stricter reader added the bug, and the fix makes it skip comment lines the way git does.

The two failures in `mise run check` were a different thing: 10-second timeouts in hook-install and external-agent tests under full-suite load. Both pass when run alone, and this PR doesn't touch either area.

Commit, push and the PR text are still waiting on your go-ahead.

content.content:
## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

I merged current main into this branch first, so the call sites below were main's code when these failed:

- `integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` drives the real prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hook binaries. `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_IndentedLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingExistingCheckpoint` and `TestTrailerAuthority_AgentCommitWithBodyLine` failed with `prepare-commit-msg must stamp a trailer in the final block`. `TestTrailerAuthority_VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` is a guard: it passes before and after, and fails if the editor-message cleanup is skipped.
- `TestAttach_BodyCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint`, `TestAttach_IndentedCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestAttach_CheckpointMentionedInProseDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` failed with `attach wrote the session into checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6, which the commit only mentions in its body`.
- `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` failed with `references checkpoint deadbeefcafe via its Entire-Checkpoint trailer: checkpoint not found`. `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` guards discovery.
- The subject-paragraph cases in `trailers_test.go` failed before that rule was added.
- `TestTrailerAuthority_EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar` and `TestTrailerAuthority_AmendHonorsCommentChar` (`;` and `auto`) failed: the recorded commit kept Entire's explanation and ended without a trailer block, and the amend appended a second trailer. `TestTrailerAuthority_ProseScissorsMarkerIsNotACut` failed with `prepare-commit-msg must stamp a trailer in the final block`, and `TestAttach_NoSpaceTrailerJoinsCheckpoint` with `attach wrote the session into <new id>, want the trailer's checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6`.
- `TestTrailerAuthority_UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` (`;` and `commit -v`) failed with `commit-msg must remove the trailer so git aborts the empty commit`, and `TestTrailerAuthority_MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer` with `commit-msg must keep the trailer of a message with content`. Its default-prefix case is a guard.
- `TestTrailerAuthority_CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` (`commit.cleanup=scissors` with `#` and `;`, and `whitespace`) failed with `post-commit must condense into the checkpoint the commit's trailer names`, while `git interpret-trailers --parse` read the trailer in each case. `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint` failed with `attach wrote the session into <new id>, want the trailer's checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6`, and the comment-line cases in `trailers_test.go` failed before the reader skipped comment lines.

# Working Agreement

These instructions apply across repositories and agent tools. Explicit user
instructions and more specific repository instructions take precedence.

## Communication

- Use direct, understandable language.
- Be concise for routine work. Be comprehensive when explaining a difficult
  concept or consequential decision.
- When teaching, build intuition with concrete examples and alternative
  perspectives. Ask a short question or offer an exercise when active practice
  would improve understanding.
- Do not use em dashes in generated content such as emails, documentation, or
  application copy. Chat replies and code are exempt.

## Reading My Prompts

- I often dictate prompts. Focus on the intended meaning even when wording,
  punctuation, or terminology is rough.
- Infer the desired outcome from the request, conversation, and relevant project
  context.
- Resolve routine uncertainty by inspecting available context and making
  reasonable, reversible decisions.
- Ask only when a missing answer would materially change the result and cannot
  be inferred safely.

## Scope

- Complete the requested outcome with the smallest sufficient change.
- Explicit user instructions override these defaults.
- Inspect the relevant code, call paths, and project conventions before editing.
  Do not explore the entire repository for a small change.
- Prefer existing code and patterns, then standard-library or built-in platform
  capabilities, then dependencies already installed. Add new dependencies only
  when the existing options are insufficient.
- Fix the governing rule or root cause, not only the example that exposed it.
- Do not add abstractions, compatibility layers, configuration, or future-only
  features that the current task does not require.
- Fix nearby issues only when they block the requested work. Otherwise, report
  them separately.
- Remove replaced implementations. Preserve an old path only when compatibility
  is explicitly required.
- Preserve necessary validation, error handling, security, accessibility, and
  user-facing behavior.

## Approval and Decisions

- Work independently within the authorized scope. Do not repeatedly ask whether
  to continue.
- Before editing any repository file, give the user a pre-edit brief that states:
  - the observed problem or requested behavior;
  - the evidence-backed root cause, or that the cause is still unknown; and
  - the proposed change, its scope, and any meaningful tradeoffs.
- Wait for the user's explicit approval of the proposed change before editing.
  A request to fix or implement something authorizes investigation, but it does
  not approve a proposal that the user has not seen.
- Until the user approves the proposal, restrict work to read-only investigation
  and reproduction that does not modify repository files. If the root cause
  remains unknown, continue investigating or ask for approval for a specific
  diagnostic edit.
- The user may explicitly waive this checkpoint.
- Ask before material scope expansion, public publication, meaningful external
  cost, destructive or irreversible actions, or decisions that would materially
  change the requested outcome.
- When I ask for a draft, comment, message, or description, show me the full
  final text first. Do not post, send, or publish it until I approve that exact
  text. If the text changes after approval, show the new version and ask again.
  This covers PR and issue comments, reviews, PR descriptions, Trail
  discussions and descriptions, commit messages written for me to review,
  emails, and chat messages.
- If multiple approaches have meaningful tradeoffs, compare them, recommend one,
  and ask for the decision.
- If the request is only to analyze, explain, or review, do not edit files.

## Testing

- NEVER write unit tests after writing the production code.
- Prefer end-to-end tests as the sole testing mechanism for complex features.
  Exercise the real user-facing workflow and produce a repeatable, inspectable
  artifact.
- If a system must be tested in isolation, first enumerate the meaningful ways
  it can fail, then write the unit tests, and only then write the production
  code.
- Do not backfill unit tests after implementation merely to increase coverage.
- Reuse existing tests before adding new ones.
- Add tests for behavior and regression risks, not tests that mechanically
  repeat implementation details.
- Temporary verification scripts do not need to become permanent test files.

## Reviewing Changes

- When I ask to review a PR, Trail, branch, or diff, explain it before judging
  it. Open with a short brief written for someone who has not read the diff:
  what the change does from the user's point of view, why it exists (the
  product or operational need), how it works at a high level, and what it
  means for performance, compatibility, data, and risk. Say what is uncertain.
- Gather intent before judging: run `entire why` or `entire blame` on the
  central changed lines, follow cited checkpoints with
  `entire checkpoint explain`, run `entire search` for earlier decisions in the
  same area, and use `entire graph impact` on changed symbols. Name the lookups
  that informed the brief, or state the evidence gap.
- For entireio and entirehq repositories, also run `librarian query --json`
  with the ticket id or PR title to find the Linear issue and Slack discussion
  behind the change, and cite them in the brief.
- Then review the diff and report findings. Keep the brief and the findings as
  separate parts of one reply.
- Skip the brief only when I say so, for example "just review it".

## Learning From Reviews

- Reviews are a chance to learn, but not every review produces a lesson. This
  covers reviews run in a session (`/review`, `/code-review`) and reviews from
  people on a PR or Trail.
- Review lessons live in
  `~/Documents/Obsidian/Life OS/Work/Entire/Review Lessons/`: `General.md` for
  lessons that apply anywhere, and `<repo>.md` for one repository, named after
  the GitHub repository (for example, `cli.md`).
- After a review, decide whether anything in it is worth keeping. Save a lesson
  only if it would change how I write or review code in a future change, and it
  is not already covered by an existing lesson, a lint rule, a type, or a test.
  Skip one-off fixes, style nits, and anything specific to this diff.
- When nothing qualifies, say so in one line and move on.
- Write each lesson as a rule with its reason, for example: "Do not use
  `unwrap` in request handlers; a panic drops the request. Return the service
  error type instead."
- Show me the proposed lessons and which file each belongs in. Add them only
  after I approve, creating the file if needed.
- Keep each file a short checklist: sharpen an existing lesson instead of
  duplicating it, merge overlapping lessons, and when a lint rule, type, or
  test can enforce a lesson, propose that change and remove the lesson.
- Before committing or opening a PR, and during any review, read `General.md`
  and the current repository's file if they exist, and check the diff against
  each lesson. Report any violation and fix it before publishing.

## Doing the Work

- Carry the task through implementation, integration, and relevant verification.
- An intermediate artifact, passing build, or list of findings is complete only
  when it satisfies the requested outcome.
- Make clear, small fixes directly. Write a short plan only when the approach is
  unclear or the impact is substantial.
- Keep implementing, verifying, and fixing within the authorized scope.
- If the plan grows into future-only layers, unrelated refactoring, or extra
  features, return to the current requirement and remove the excess work.
- Keep explanations concise without shortening the actual work.

## Verification

- Verify the result in the way it will actually be used. Tests and builds are
  evidence, not substitutes for the requested outcome.
- For visual work, inspect the rendered result in its intended context. Check the
  relevant states and interactions.
- For performance work, measure the actual bottleneck first. Compare the same
  workload before and after, report the numbers and tradeoffs, and preserve
  behavior.
- Fix issues found during verification and run the relevant check again.
- Before finishing, compare the result with the original request and later
  corrections.
- Report what was verified, what was not verified, and why.
- If something remains blocked, state exactly what is unfinished and what
  prevents completion.

## Code Quality

- Prefer self-explanatory code.
- Add a comment only for a non-obvious invariant, constraint, safety reason,
  protocol quirk, or public contract that clearer code cannot express.
- Keep comments short and explain why the logic is necessary. Do not narrate
  obvious operations or restate the code.
- Never put agent names, task names or IDs, ticket IDs, phase labels, session
  notes, implementation chronology, or review-process metadata in source
  comments or documentation comments.
- Keep planning, tracking, and handoff context in issues, commits, pull requests,
  or local coordination files rather than production code.
- Remove stale or process-oriented comments when touching nearby code.

## Constructor Design

- Constructors should be cheap and predictable.
- Primary or critical constructors may perform eager fallible setup when the
  failure is returned explicitly.
- Non-critical subsystems such as telemetry, metrics, and logging must not break
  their caller. Initialize them lazily or on a best-effort basis.
- Never hide fallible work behind an infallible constructor. If construction can
  fail materially, return the language's explicit error type.
- Apply this rule across languages and resources, including database pools, HTTP
  clients, file handles, and background tasks.

## Delegation

- Handle small, tightly scoped work directly.
- When delegation is available, delegate substantial independent work only when
  it improves speed, coverage, or confidence.
- Give delegated agents a bounded objective, relevant context, expected output,
  and verification requirement.
- Do not delegate merely to create activity.
- The primary agent remains responsible for decisions, integration, and final
  verification.

## Personal Workspace

- `~/hub` is the source of truth for personal machine configuration, universal
  agent instructions, reusable workflows, and automation.
- `~/hub/AGENTS.md` is the universal instruction source. The installer links it
  into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Delta; edit the source, not those links.
- `~/hub/configs/` contains GNU Stow packages for agent configuration only
  (Claude Code wrapper, Codex profile). General dotfiles, including shell
  functions that call hub, live in `~/dotfiles`. Edit files in the package that owns them rather than
  editing the linked path under `$HOME`.
  Content edits propagate through existing links; rerun the relevant installer
  scope only when links or package paths change.
- `~/hub/skills/` contains judgment-heavy, explicitly user-invoked workflows.
  Use `/skill-name`; do not turn deterministic mechanics into native skills.
- `~/hub/scripts/` contains deterministic user commands and is on `PATH`. Use
  `$ command` notation when recommending one. Agent-routable commands are
  declared in `~/hub/scripts/actions.json`.
- `~/hub/tools/` contains implementation packages behind commands. They are not
  user-facing and must not re-enter the skill catalog.
- Retired skills are deleted, not archived; recover one from Git history only
  after reviewing it against current workflows and adding routing coverage.
- Reusable prompts live in `~/Documents/Obsidian/Life OS/Work/Entire/` as
  `<Name> Prompt.md`. When I ask for a saved prompt, look there.
- Read `~/Documents/Obsidian/Life OS/Work/Entire/Agent Memory.md` at the start
  of every task. When you learn how I like to work, propose adding it there
  rather than to a repo's memory. Repo memory is only for facts about that repo.
- Before working in an Entire code area, check `Learnings/Index.md` in the
  same folder for past investigations of it.
- When changing the action catalog, keep `skills/README.md`,
  `scripts/README.md`, `scripts/actions.json`, routing evals, and layout tests in
  sync. Regenerate the skill index with `scripts/generate-skills-index`.
### Entire Before Guessing

Entire provides recorded intent, provenance, session history, structural code
navigation, and (with Entire Brain) durable facts distilled from past sessions.
Git remains authoritative for the current working tree and branch state.

After a task is authorized, use applicable read-only Entire commands directly as
evidence gathering. This does not require another skill-selection step. Because
commands vary by version and repository, use `entire agent-help [COMMAND] --json`
instead of guessing unsupported syntax.

For the questions below, run the matching Entire command before `git log`,
`git blame`, `git show <commit>`, `git grep`, or `rg`. Use Git history and text
search afterward to confirm a result or fill a gap Entire reports. Text search
stays the right first tool for an exact literal string.

Choose the first tool by the question:

- **What should I know before this task?**

  When Entire Brain is available, start with:

  ```bash
  entire brain brief "<task>"
  ```

  It returns a bounded packet of relevant facts, history, and docs. Use
  `--handoff` instead when resuming a stopped session. Treat the packet as
  pointers to verify against current source, not as the answer.

- **Why does this code exist?**

  ```bash
  entire why path/to/file:LINE --json
  entire blame path/to/file:START-END --json
  ```

  Follow the cited history with
  `entire checkpoint explain ID_OR_COMMIT --short --no-pager`. Read the full
  transcript only when the summary is insufficient.

- **What was decided, or have we done this before?**

  ```bash
  entire search "<question>" --compact --limit 5
  entire brain query "<question>" --limit 5
  entire brain recall "<question>" --k 5
  ```

  `search` reads checkpoint history, `brain query` searches facts, history, and
  docs together, and `brain recall` returns only durable facts (decisions,
  invariants, gotchas, conventions) for the current branch. Widen `search` with
  `--all-repos` only when the current repository has no useful result.

- **Where is code, what calls it, or what could a change affect?**

  When Entire Graph is available, start with:

  ```bash
  entire graph search --repo . --format agent --top-k 5 --query "<task>"
  entire graph def SYMBOL --repo .
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol SYMBOL
  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol SYMBOL
  ```

  Then inspect the cited source and run focused tests. Read a known small file
  directly instead of invoking Graph.
  Graph indexes the checked-out tree. When the revision under review is not
  checked out, say so and inspect that revision with Git.

- **Continue previous work?**

  ```bash
  entire session current --json
  entire session list --json
  entire checkpoint list --pending --json
  ```

  Inspect first. Use `entire session resume` only when actually restoring a
  stopped session, and do not use `--force` casually.

- **The branch has an Entire Trail?**

  When Trail commands are available, resolve the exact repository and branch,
  then read context without resuming. A Trail is project-wide: a bare number
  names the project trail, and `<repo>/<number>` names its change in one
  repository, which still resolves after a merge deletes the branch:

  ```bash
  entire trail show --branch "<branch>" --repo "gh/<owner>/<repo>" --json
  entire trail resume "<repo>/<number>" --no-resume --json
  ```

  Read this context before syncing, merging, rebasing, committing, or publishing
  the branch. Use Git for the actual branch operation.

Use Git first for `status`, uncommitted changes, staging, exact diffs, refs,
remotes, fetch, merge, rebase, commit, and push. Entire Search cannot see
uncommitted, local-only, or unindexed work.

Keep lookups bounded and verify Entire results against current source. Historical
context records what was intended at the time, not necessarily what the code does
now. If Entire is unavailable or has no relevant history, state the evidence gap
and continue with Git and source inspection.

Do not use `entire checkpoint explain --generate` for normal investigation
because it writes a summary and spends provider tokens.

### Repository Workflow

- Work in one branch and worktree per concern. Keep the primary checkout on a
  clean, current default branch; do not implement features or review PRs there.
- For bare-clone repositories under `~/Work` (`.bare` + worktrees), including

<pasted_content id="730c">
Regressions against main

1. An aborted editor amend gets committed with only the trailer (cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:206).
   - Mechanism: commit-msg skips the comment prefix whenever the last line is an Entire-Checkpoint: trailer. The amend restore path (handleAmendCommitMsg, line 883) adds its trailer after git's # comment block.
   - Trigger: git commit --amend, then the user deletes the subject to abort. The # lines now count as content, so the trailer isn't removed and git records a commit whose message is just Entire-Checkpoint: X.
   - On main: # lines were always skipped, so the amend aborted.
   - stampFreshCheckpointForAmend has the same problem.
2. Typing on the blank line in the editor template loses the link (manual_commit_hooks.go:2917).
   - Mechanism: addCheckpointTrailerWithComment leaves only one blank line above the trailer. If the user types on that line, the subject runs straight into the trailer, e.g. subject\nEntire-Checkpoint: X.
   - Effect: finalTrailerBlock rejects a block that starts at line 0 (the subject paragraph), so post-commit never condenses. The commit keeps a trailer that points at nothing.
   - On main: ParseAllCheckpoints still found the trailer.
3. core.commentChar=auto misreads the comment character (manual_commit_hooks.go:2832).
   - Mechanism: recordedCommentPrefix maps auto to #. But when the message has a line starting with #, git picks ;, and prepare writes its explanation lines with ;.
   - Effect: With a cleanup mode that keeps comments (scissors), those ; lines stay in the trailer block. The block is then no longer a valid trailer block, so post-commit, attach and explain --generate all miss the trailer.

Older bug in a function the PR touches

4. A restored amend trailer is cut off with commit -v (manual_commit_hooks.go:883).
   - Mechanism: The amend restore and stampFreshCheckpointForAmend use addCheckpointTrailer, which appends at the very end of the message. With commit -v that is below the scissors line, which git discards, so the amend silently loses its link.
   - Fix: addInheritedCheckpointTrailer(message, cpID, gitCommentPrefix(ctx, message)) already places the trailer correctly.

Correctness gaps in the new final-block rule

I checked all eight findings. Findings 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 are regressions against main that this branch introduced (1 and 8 by the earlier commit-msg change, 2, 3 and 5 by the stricter final-block reader). Finding 4 is older and gets fixed with 1. Findings 6 and 7 behave the same as on main. Here's the evidence, then what I propose.

## What each finding comes to

| # | Real? | Regression vs main? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Aborted editor amend commits a trailer-only message | Yes | Yes, from the commit-msg change in 4cfd66130 | Restore, fresh-stamp and the agent fast path append the trailer after git's `#` block. commit-msg then sees a trailer as the last line, treats it as a `-m` message, and counts the `#` lines as content. |
| 2. Subject typed on the blank line above the trailer loses the link | Yes | Yes | The template is `\n\n` + trailer. Real git records `subject\nEntire-Checkpoint: X` as one paragraph (the subject), and `interpret-trailers` reads no trailer. Post-commit skips it; main's whole-message scan found it. |
| 3. `auto` plus scissors misreads the prefix | Yes, narrow | Yes | It needs `auto`, a comment-keeping cleanup mode, and a `#` line in the message. Prepare writes `;` lines inside the trailer paragraph, and the recorded-commit reader skips `#`. |
| 4. Restored amend trailer lost with `commit -v` | Yes | No, older | The same append-at-end lands below the scissors line. |
| 5. Reader stricter than git | Yes | Yes | Git 2.50 reads the trailer in a `cherry-pick -x` block (`(cherry picked from …)` line) and in a block that is at least 25% trailers and has a `Signed-off-by:`. Ours rejects both, so a `-x` cherry-pick acts unlinked while a plain cherry-pick acts linked. |
| 6. GitHub squash merge joins the last squashed checkpoint | Yes | No | Main's attach also took the last ID. By git's grammar that trailer is the commit's final block, so this rule can't tell the difference. |
| 7. `explain --generate` picks the first trailer, attach the last | Yes | No | Main's `ParseCheckpoint` also took the first. |
| 8. `commit.cleanup=strip` with `-m "#42 fix"` | Yes, narrow | Yes, from 4cfd66130 | Real git with `strip` drops the `#42 fix` line from an `-m` message too and records a commit containing only `Entire-Checkpoint: X`. Main's commit-msg removed the trailer, so git aborted. |

## Proposed fixes for this PR

Each fix gets a failing test first, through the real hooks where it can.

1. **Findings 1 and 4:** write the restored amend trailer, the fresh amend trailer and the editor fast-path trailer above git's comment block. The squash/redo helper already does this; I'd rename it to say what it does (`addCheckpointTrailerAboveComments`) and use it at those 3 sites. The commit-msg rule "a trailer at the end means `-m`" then holds again for everything Entire writes.
2. **Findings 2 and 3:** change the editor template to put the explanation above the trailer, each in its own paragraph:
   ```
   <subject line>

   # Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer below if you don't want to link …
   # Last Prompt: …
   # The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.

   Entire-Checkpoint: X

   # Please enter the commit message…
   ```
   Typing on either blank line above can't run into the trailer, because the explanation and a blank line separate them. In scissors mode the explanation no longer sits in the trailer's paragraph, so finding 3 goes away without a special case for `auto`.
   - **Tradeoff:** a visible template change, and the text now says "below".
   - **Not fixed:** under scissors the explanation still ends up in the commit, as on main.
3. **Finding 5:** follow git's rule. A block also counts if it has a `Signed-off-by: ` or `(cherry picked from commit ` line and is at least 25% trailers. That's about 20 lines in `isTrailerBlock`, unit-tested against git's outputs first, and it makes `-x` cherry-picks behave like plain ones (and like main).
4. **Finding 7:** `explain --generate` takes the last final-block trailer, like attach. One line.

## Proposed to document, not fix

New "Known gap" sentences, text for your approval later:
- **Finding 6:** fixing it needs a separate way to recognize squash merges, and main behaves the same.
- **Finding 8:** a fix needs `commit.cleanup` plumbing plus a `git config` spawn on every `-m` commit (agents commit this way). It still can't see `git commit --cleanup=…`, and the case is a message made only of comment lines, which git itself would strip.

The alternative for 2 and 3: post-commit could trust the ID prepare stamped wherever it ends up, recorded in a marker the way inherited trailers are. That's more general but adds state, so I'd go with the template change. Nothing is edited yet.

func TestTrailerAuthority_VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
	authorityAgentTurn(env, "mine.txt", "my agent work\n")
	env.GitCommitWithHooks("My change", "mine.txt")
	headMsg := env.GetCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
	require.NotEmpty(t, trailers.ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock(headMsg, ""), "precondition: HEAD is linked: %q", headMsg)

	amendMsg := strings.TrimRight(headMsg, "\n") + "\n\n" +
		"# Please enter the commit message for your changes. Lines starting\n" +
		"# with '#' will be ignored, and an empty message aborts the commit.\n" +
		"#\n" +
		"# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\n" +
		"# Do not modify or remove the line above.\n" +
		"# Everything below it will be ignored.\n" +
		"diff --git a/mine.txt b/mine.txt\n" +
		"--- a/mine.txt\n" +
		"+++ b/mine.txt\n" +
		"@@ -0,0 +1 @@\n" +
		"+my agent work\n"
	_, prepared := runPrepareCommitMsg(env, amendMsg, "commit")
	require.Equal(t, amendMsg, prepared, "the amend keeps the commit's own trailer and adds none")
}

func TestTrailerAuthority_UntouchedEditorMessageAborts(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	tests := []struct {
		name        string
		commentChar string
		message     string // as git hands it to prepare-commit-msg
	}{
		// GUARD: the default prefix.
		{name: "default prefix", message: "\n" + gitCommentBlock("#")},
		{name: "semicolon", commentChar: ";", message: "\n" + gitCommentBlock(";")},
		{
			name: "verbose",
			message: "\n" + gitCommentBlock("#") +
				"# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\n" +
				"# Do not modify or remove the line above.\n" +
				"# Everything below it will be ignored.\n" +
				"diff --git a/mine.txt b/mine.txt\n" +
				"+my agent work\n",
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
			if tt.commentChar != "" {
				setRepoGitConfig(env, "core.commentChar", tt.commentChar)
			}
			authorityAgentTurn(env, "mine.txt", "my agent work\n")
			env.GitAdd("mine.txt")
			msgFile, prepared := runPrepareCommitMsg(env, tt.message, "")
			require.NotEmpty(t, trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(prepared), "precondition: prepare stamped a trailer: %q", prepared)

			// The user saves without typing anything.
			edited := runCommitMsgHook(env, msgFile)

			require.Empty(t, trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(edited),
				"commit-msg must remove the trailer so git aborts the empty commit: %q", edited)
		})

path that writes to a checkpoint because a commit names it reads the commit's
final trailer block by git's grammar: no leading whitespace, indented lines
only as continuations of a trailer, lines starting with git's comment prefix
skipped (trailing comment lines too), other lines allowed only in a block
holding a line git generates (`Signed-off-by: `, `(cherry picked from commit `)
and at most three per trailer line, and never the subject paragraph. An
`Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere else in the message (pasted, quoted,
indented, or mentioned in prose) names a checkpoint the commit did not stamp,
so prepare-commit-msg stamps a fresh trailer and post-commit condenses there.
Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor message loses the
lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the scissors line
down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is
`core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases; the last one set wins),
`#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote
into the message. Every trailer prepare adds to an editor message goes above
git's comment block, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off, and commit-msg still
sees the comment block that marks an editor message. The editor template puts
prepare's explanation, written with the same prefix, in its own paragraph
between the user's lines and the trailer: a line typed just above the trailer
cannot join the subject paragraph, and `commit.cleanup` modes that keep comment
lines leave the trailer as its own block. A recorded commit is read with the
configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as `git interpret-trailers` does).
Read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, read-only explain) and squash
and redo inheritance still scan the whole message, because squash commits carry
their squashed commits' trailers in the body. The trailer writer joins only a
block of trailer lines alone, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers
accept.

"""
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Findings 1–5 and 7 are fixed locally (10 files, +385/−111). Each test failed before its fix and passes after. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted yet.

**What changed:**
- **Findings 1 and 4:** an amend's restored or fresh trailer, and an agent's editor-commit trailer, now go above git's comment block instead of after the diff.
- **Findings 2 and 3:** the editor template now writes Entire's explanation in its own paragraph above the trailer.
  - That change made a `commit.status=false` editor message end with the trailer, so commit-msg would have kept the trailer instead of aborting an untouched commit. commit-msg now treats Entire's explanation as the sign of an editor message. A guard test covers it.
- **Finding 5:** the reader follows git's rule for blocks containing a `Signed-off-by:` or cherry-pick note. The writer still joins only blocks that are pure trailers, so an existing #2259 test keeps its behavior.
- **Finding 7:** `explain --generate` takes the last trailer.
- **One more fix found while checking:** both writers used to insert before the *first* comment-prefixed line. An amend body or template with a `#` line mid-way then put the trailer above text git keeps, so it wasn't the final block. They now anchor to the comment block that ends the message, and two new unit tests cover it.

**Verification:**
- **Failing first:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (3 cases), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` scissors row, the two `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` tests, 3 grammar cases plus a writer case, and the explain test.
- **`mise run check`:** lint has 0 issues and 91 packages pass. Four tests in the hook-install and external-command-signal areas timed out under load. Each passes alone, and this PR doesn't touch either area.
- **Not covered:** `git commit --amend --no-edit` restoring a trailer into a message made *only* of `#` lines would put the trailer first. I left it, because it needs the restore path plus an all-comment message.

**Proposed commit message:**
```
fix(trailers): keep prepare's trailers in the block git reads

The final-block rule could still drop links the whole-message scan kept:

- An amend's restored or fresh trailer, and an agent's editor-commit
  trailer, were appended after git's comment block. commit -v cut them
  off with the diff, and commit-msg read the message as -m, so clearing
  an amend to abort it recorded a commit holding only the trailer. They
  now go above the comment block, as inherited trailers do.
- The editor template put the trailer right below the typing lines, so a
  subject typed on the second line joined it into the subject paragraph,
  which git never reads as trailers. Prepare's explanation now sits
  between them in its own paragraph, which also keeps the comment lines
  commit.cleanup=scissors leaves, in any prefix, out of the trailer
  block. commit-msg reads that explanation as the mark of an editor
  message, so an untouched commit.status=false message still aborts.
- The reader rejected blocks git accepts: a cherry-pick -x note, or
  other lines in a block with a Signed-off-by: line while trailers make
  up a quarter of it. It now follows git's rule; the writer still joins
  only blocks of trailers alone.

Both writers find git's comment block as the run of comment lines that
ends the message, so a "#" line in a kept body or a template no longer
pulls the trailer above lines git keeps. explain --generate writes into
the block's last trailer, the one attach joins, not the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Proposed PR description changes:**

1. **Fix section, new paragraph** before "The commit-msg hook's empty-message check…":
   > Every trailer prepare adds to an editor message goes above the comment block that ends it, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins.
2. **The commit-msg paragraph in the same section:** replace "an editor message ends with git's comment block and a `-m`/`-F` message ends with its own text, so prefix lines count as comments only when that block ends the message," with:
   > an editor message ends with git's comment block or carries prepare's explanation, and a `-m`/`-F` message has neither, so prefix lines count as comments only in an editor message,
3. **Tests section, after the guards line:**
   > Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:
   >
   > - **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
   > - **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
4. **Known gap, two new paragraphs** (findings 6 and 8):
   > A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.
   >
   > With `commit.cleanup=strip`, git also removes comment lines from a `-m` message, which commit-msg counts as kept, so `git commit -m "#42 fix"` is recorded with only its trailer instead of aborting. Fixing it needs `commit.cleanup` read on every `-m` commit, and `git commit --cleanup=…` would still go unseen.

content.text:
Of the 8 trail findings, I fixed 6 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7) and documented 2 (6 and 8) under "Known gap" in the PR. None were dismissed as wrong: all 8 held up against the code and real git.

**Fixed (in `52ae5ec22`):**

| # | Finding | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Aborted editor amend committed with only the trailer | The restored and fresh amend trailers, and the agent fast-path trailer, now go above git's comment block. commit-msg sees an editor message again, so clearing the amend aborts it. |
| 2 | Subject typed on the template's blank line loses the link | The explanation now sits above the trailer in its own paragraph, so a typed line can't join the trailer's paragraph. |
| 3 | `auto` + scissors misreads the prefix | Fixed by the same template change: the `;` explanation lines no longer sit inside the trailer block. |
| 4 | Restored amend trailer cut off by `commit -v` | Fixed with 1: the trailer lands above the scissors line. |
| 5 | Reader stricter than git | The reader now follows git's rule: a cherry-pick `-x` note, or other lines in a block with a `Signed-off-by:` line, as long as trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. The writer still joins only blocks that are all trailers. |
| 7 | `explain --generate` picks the first trailer, attach the last | It now takes the last, like attach. |

Two more things came out of those fixes:
- **Writer anchor:** both trailer writers now anchor to the comment block that *ends* the message, so a `#` line in an amend body or a template no longer pulls the trailer above text git keeps.
- **`commit.status=false` guard:** the template change would have made an untouched message with no comment block commit with just the trailer instead of aborting. commit-msg now treats Entire's own explanation as the mark of an editor message, and a guard test covers it.

**Documented, not fixed:**

| # | Finding | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | GitHub "Squash and merge" joins the last squashed checkpoint | Main behaves the same, and by git's own grammar that trailer is the commit's final block. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges. |
| 8 | `commit.cleanup=strip` + `-m "#42 fix"` records a trailer-only commit | Fixing it means a `git config` read on every `-m` commit (agents commit this way), and `--cleanup=` on the command line would still go unseen. It only happens when the message is nothing but comment lines, which git itself would strip. |

From my own review earlier, separate from these 8:
- **Fixed:** the `commit.cleanup=scissors/whitespace` link loss and the extra `git config` read on every amend (both in `f74bb0c05`).
- **Open:** the CRLF scissors-line nit, which wasn't in the approved scope.
- **Follow-up:** whole-message squash/redo inheritance is in Known gap, and the follow-up session card is still waiting.

I couldn't reach the Trail itself, so none of these 8 are marked resolved there; that needs doing on the Trail.

The upstream/main merge (`afb2a81c5`) is still in `mise run check` and isn't pushed yet. I'll push once it passes.

content.text:
The merge is pushed (`afb2a81c5`). On the new head, `test-release-origins` and `govulncheck` now pass, and the rest of CI is still running.

On your question: some of the gaps belong in this PR and some don't. The test is simple. If this PR introduced the gap, fix it here. If main already behaves the same way and the fix needs a new design, a separate PR is cleaner.

**Fix in this PR:**
- **`commit.cleanup=strip` with `-m "#42 fix"` (finding 8).** I documented this one because of its cost, but this branch introduced it (the commit-msg change in 4cfd66130), so it should be fixed here. The fix reads `commit.cleanup` in the same `git config` call that already reads the comment prefix, and treats comment lines as stripped when the mode is `strip`. The cost is one `git config` read on each `-m` commit that carries a trailer, about 3 ms. That's mostly agent commits, so the cost is real but small. Roughly 30 lines plus a test.
- **CRLF scissors line.** It's a 3-line change. The code and its comment claim the exact-scissors behavior matches git, but git 2.50 doesn't cut at a CRLF scissors line. Fixing it makes the claim true.

**Separate follow-up PR:**
- **Squash/redo whole-message inheritance and GitHub "Squash and merge" (finding 6).** I'd do these together in one follow-up:
  - **Not regressions:** main behaves exactly the same. This PR's job was to stop a body mention from steering a write *directly*, and it does that.
  - **Needs its own design:** the fix has to recognize squash messages. That means splitting SQUASH_MSG per commit, removing its indentation, and deciding what nested squashes and GitHub's format mean. That's new design with its own failure modes.
  - **Changes main's current behavior:** an existing main test (`TestPrepareCommitMsg_SquashDefaultMessageKeepsInheritedTrailerOnce`) pins how squash output looks today.
  - **Size and review cost:** it would add about 150 to 250 lines to a PR that's already large and has had three review rounds. Reviewers would have to re-review squash behavior on top of the trailer rules. A separate PR is also easier to revert or bisect on its own.

**Leave as Known gaps:**
- **`git commit -m … -e`.** Git reports source `message` even though it opens the editor, and the hook gets no other signal. A `-m` message can legitimately end with `#` lines, so guessing could break real messages. Main has the same gap.
- **`--amend --no-edit` restoring a trailer into a message made only of `#` lines.** The trailer would land first. That takes three rare conditions at once, and handling it would need yet another heuristic.

If you agree, I'll fix finding 8 and the CRLF nit here, tests first, and update the Known gap text. Squash stays as the follow-up card.

I'm planning the test cases first: checking that commit.cleanup=strip actually strips the trailer so git aborts, while confirming default cleanup still preserves it as covered by the existing subject-starting-with-hash test.

Then I work through how different cleanup modes (whitespace, verbatim, scissors, strip) interact with -m message handling—only "strip" actually removes comment lines, so only strip can disrupt trailer detection. I decide the fix should stay minimal and scoped to the commit-msg hook rather than touching prepare-commit-msg, since prepare's behavior under strip is already safe (it errs toward stamping fresh) and isn't the source of the reported regression. So commit-msg needs to be made aware of the cleanup mode when parsing the message.

I plan to extend the config lookup into something like `gitCleanupConfig`, which fetches both the comment prefix and `commit.cleanup` setting in a single `git config --get-regexp` call, then parses out the last value for each key. For commit-msg's trailer detection, I need to always spawn the prefix lookup even in the -m shape, since cleanup mode affects whether the message should be treated as having stripped comment lines.

I'm restructuring so CommitMsg always resolves the prefix, then branches: if cleanup is "strip", comments get stripped regardless of shape; otherwise it falls back to checking for editor-style comment blocks. I need to adjust `hasUserContent`'s signature so it takes the comment prefix and a flag for whether comments are being stripped, rather than inferring the shape internally.

Now I'm tracing whether git applies the scissors cut for `-m` mode specifically — recalling that git's `cleanup_message` only truncates at the scissors line when either verbose mode or scissors cleanup mode is active, and that logic seems gated behind the "use_editor" check as well, so I need to verify whether `-m` bypasses this entirely.

I'm sketching how stripping should trigger: rather than hardcoding the comment prefix for `-m`-style messages, the editor-detection logic should decide based on whether the last non-blank line matches an editor-comment pattern, so trailer-only messages like "Fix login\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: X" correctly skip stripping while comment-block messages correctly get stripped.

I'm also uncertain whether git cuts at the scissors line for `-m` messages outside interactive-edit mode, so I'm leaning toward only applying the cut when the message is editor-shaped or strip mode is active, and ordering the scissors-cut check before the editor-shape detection since that detection depends on the post-cut content.

Writing the function logic...

I'm reasoning through when git actually strips comment lines versus preserves them: strip-only happens via commit.cleanup=strip, an editor-written message loses comments by default, but a message that ends in its trailer with no prepare-commit-msg explanation behaves like it came from -m or -F, so comments should stay.

I realize the heuristic is designed for the commit-msg hook distinguishing -m from editor input, but it misjudges the edge case where a user deletes git's comment block in the editor and types only prefix-style lines — git still strips those as comments in edit mode, while the heuristic would read them as content. That's an accepted, documented limitation rather than something I need to fix.

With explicit cleanup=strip configured, git strips prefix lines in every mode, so hasUserContent should strip unconditionally when stripsComments is true, only falling back to the heuristic (checking the last non-blank line or trailer explanation) otherwise. comment prefix and treats comment lines as dropped under strip. That
call now runs for every commit that carries a trailer, -m ones included.

The scissors cut no longer accepts a CRLF line: git cuts only at a line
ended by "\n" alone, and keeps the diff below a CRLF one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
Finding 8 and the CRLF nit are fixed locally (5 files, +75/−38), tests first. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted yet.

**What changed:**
- **Finding 8:** commit-msg reads `commit.cleanup` in the same `git config` call as the comment prefix. Under `strip` it treats comment lines as dropped in every message, so `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` now aborts. The tradeoff: commit-msg now does that one config read on every commit carrying a trailer, `-m` included. Before, it skipped the read for `-m` messages.
- **CRLF:** the scissors check accepts only a line ended by `\n`, matching git.

**Verification:**
- **Failed first:** `TestTrailerAuthority_StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts` and the CRLF case in `TestStripEditorComments`. Both pass now.
- **Guards still pass:** `-m "#42 fix login"` keeps its trailer under default cleanup, and untouched editor messages abort.
- **`mise run check`:** lint 0 issues, 92 packages pass. Two Claude Code agent tests hit their 5 s limit and pass alone; that code is identical to upstream main.

**Proposed commit message:**
```
fix(strategy): honor commit.cleanup=strip in commit-msg's empty check

With commit.cleanup=strip git drops comment lines from -m messages too,
so `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` leaves nothing. commit-msg read a
message ending with its trailer as -m and kept the "#" line as content,
so git recorded a commit holding only the trailer instead of aborting.
commit-msg now reads commit.cleanup in the same git config call as the
comment prefix and treats comment lines as dropped under strip. That
call now runs for every commit that carries a trailer, -m ones included.

The scissors cut no longer accepts a CRLF line: git cuts only at a line
ended by "\n" alone, and keeps the diff below a CRLF one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Proposed PR description changes:**
1. **Fix section, commit-msg paragraph:** after "…using the same comment prefix and exact scissors line.", add:
   > Under `commit.cleanup=strip`, which git applies to `-m` messages too, they count as comments in every message.
2. **Tests section, new bullet** in the "Review then found regressions…" list:
   > - **`commit.cleanup=strip` and scissors:** `StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts`, and the CRLF scissors case in `trailers_test.go`, where git does not cut.
3. **Known gap:** remove the `commit.cleanup=strip` paragraph, since it's fixed now. The `-m … -e`, squash/redo and GitHub squash-merge paragraphs stay.
